newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks post modest gains in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks post modest gains in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were slightly firmer in Thursday morning trade but foreign funds wiped out an early leap of 120 points in the Hang Seng Index, traders said.
"There's no corporate news to explain this," said David Williamson at W.I. Carr. "The market should be higher but selling orders, particularly from Europe, are bringing it down."
The Hang Seng was up 34.93 points at 13,320.36 after jumping to an early high of 13,405.54. Turnover was HK$3.06 billion after the first hour of trade.
Dealers said short-covering, the expiry of the January Hang Seng index future and improved U.S. bonds should provide support for the Hang Seng through the morning session.

Friendly economic data in the United States and a well-received auction of inflation-indexed bonds pushed the U.S. benchmark 30-year bond yield to 6.91 percent on Wednesday from 6.93 percent on Tuesday.

Dealers said the market is watching the U.S. long bond closely for any sign of a U.S. rate move at next week's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy-making arm of the U.S. Federal Reserve.
Dealers said Hong Kong stocks should also receive technical support following Wednesday's sharp slide, when the Hang Seng Index shed 117.86 points to 13,285.43.
Among active issues, GZI Transport debuted at HK$4.50 per share against an issue price of HK$3.23. The stock soon rose to HK$4.725 in heavy turnover.

Dealers said they were also watching property stocks for a rebound following weakness on Wednesday. Sun Hung Kai Properties was up HK$0.75 at HK$89.50, Henderson Land gained HK$0.25 to HK$72.72 and Cheung Kong rose HK$0.50 to HK$72.75. The Hang Seng property sub-index was up 100 points at 25,349.
